evals.name: audit-manuscript
evals.prompt: Check whether the citations in paper.tex support their claims.
evals.expected_output: A citation audit classifying: the Transformer 28.4 BLEU claim as supported; the Transformer needs-more-compute claim as unsupported (the paper states a fraction of prior training costs); the BERT GLUE-80.5-plus-annotation-costs claim as partially supported (cost half unaddressed); the Snow et al. non-expert-quality claim as supported; the kellner2021 claim as unverifiable (key resolves to no work). The manuscript and bibliography are not edited; a dated ledger is written at literature/verifications.md; every verdict earned from a retrieved source quotes evidence with a resolvable locator, while the unverifiable kellner2021 entry records explicit none sentinels instead of invented evidence.
assertions: Transformer BLEU-28.4 claim is classified supported, quoting the paper's 28.4 BLEU statement as evidence
Transformer needs-more-training-compute claim is classified unsupported, citing the paper's 'fraction of the training costs' statement as the contradiction
BERT GLUE-80.5-plus-annotation-costs claim is classified partially supported, naming the annotation-cost half as unaddressed by the paper
Snow et al. non-expert-quality claim is classified supported with evidence from the retrieved paper
kellner2021 claim is classified unverifiable because the key resolves to no bibliography entry (not unsupported)
paper.tex and refs.bib in the host copy are byte-identical to the fixtures (nothing was edited)
Host copy contains literature/verifications.md with dated entries covering the checked claims
Report separates findings from proposals (an Author decisions section exists and no change is applied)

evals.name: bib-audit
evals.prompt: Audit the bibliography metadata in refs.bib -- I want to know whether each entry identifies a real work and whether the fields are right.
evals.expected_output: An entry-level audit classifying: sheng2008 as confirmed (clean Crossref record); vaswani2017 as discrepant (entry year 2018 vs registrar 2017; correction proposed, not applied); liu2019 as mismatched (its DOI resolves to Devlin et al., NAACL 2019, a different work); snow2008 as discrepant (Crossref DOI 10.3115/1613715.1613751 exists though the Anthology page omits it; the DOI is proposed as an addition); ramanathan2014 as unconfirmed, phrased as a question for the author rather than a fabrication verdict. refs.bib is not edited; bib: ledger entries are appended.
assertions: sheng2008 is classified confirmed against its registrar record
vaswani2017 is classified discrepant, with the year 2018-vs-2017 difference reported as a proposed correction (not applied)
liu2019 is classified mismatched, with the report stating its DOI actually resolves to the Devlin et al. NAACL 2019 paper
snow2008 is classified discrepant with its Crossref DOI (10.3115/1613715.1613751) proposed as an addition, not applied
ramanathan2014 is classified unconfirmed and raised as a question for the author, not ruled fabricated on registrar absence alone
refs.bib in the host copy is byte-identical to the fixture (nothing was edited)
Host copy contains a ledger with dated bib: entries for the audited references
Report has the three bibliography-audit sections: Scope and lookups, Bibliography audit, Author decisions

evals.name: uncited-claim
evals.prompt: Find a source I could cite for this claim in my notes (notes.md): 'It is well known that repeated labeling improves label quality when annotators are noisy.'
evals.expected_output: At least one on-topic candidate source (e.g., Sheng, Provost & Ipeirotis, KDD 2008, doi:10.1145/1401890.1401965, or comparable repeated-labeling work) offered as a proposal with a resolvable locator and a quoted supporting passage from text actually retrieved. Nothing is inserted into notes.md; an uncited ledger entry is appended with the claim hash and search scope.
assertions: At least one on-topic candidate source about repeated labeling / label quality is offered with a resolvable DOI or URL
A supporting passage is quoted from text that was actually retrieved during the run (not asserted from memory)
notes.md in the host copy is byte-identical to the fixture (no citation was inserted)
The candidate is presented as a proposal for the author to adopt, not applied automatically
Host copy contains a ledger with a dated uncited entry recording the claim and the search performed
